== 1. THE STANDING REJECTION IS DISCHARGED, AND THIS IS THE FIRST ROW TODAY WHOSE COMPLETION COMMIT ACTUALLY CARRIES ITS DELIVERABLE ==
Rejected for: "no recorded completion commit contains the canonical authority-body extraction… two owned paths remain modified and four extracted module/bridge paths remain untracked".

That is the timestamp artifact of recording a pre-existing commit, not an absent delivery, and my bar permits approving over it only because I verified HEAD myself — the five measurements above are that verification.

== 2. DoD 2 — LINE COUNTS ==
compiled-authority-bodies.ts 131, compiled-approval-authority-body.ts 128, compiled-policy-authority-body.ts 198. Every production source under the 250 target, not merely under the 400 cap. The test file is 260 lines and is not held to the production cap.

== 3. DoD 3 — BYTE IDENTITY. THE PART THAT ALMOST PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON ==
FIRST, WHAT IS GOOD: the oracle is genuinely independent. `EXPECTED` is a frozen literal block of byte counts and sha256 digests (resultBytes 8563 / resultSha256 d86a47c1…, planBytes 697 / 4fd94baf…, acceptanceBytes 912 / 74b89a2b…, graphBytes 5019 / 044ffdb9…), plus full literal JSON strings for the plan and acceptance bytes and a base64 literal for the graph. Nothing is imported from or derived from the module under test, so no single edit moves both sides. The surface is pinned as set equality — `expect(Object.keys(compiledAuthorityNamespace)).toEqual(["compiledPlanAuthority"])` — and freezing is pinned position by position as `[true, false, true, true, true, true]`.
THEN THE PROBLEM. A golden is only a REGRESSION oracle if it predates the change. It does not here:
  `git show 95575b34^:…compiled-authority-bodies.test.ts | grep -c <digest>` returns **0 for every one** of the five goldens, and the entire `EXPECTED` block (resultBytes/planBytes/acceptanceBytes/graphBytes) is ABSENT pre-split.
  So the goldens were INTRODUCED BY the split commit itself. On their own they certify only that the current implementation is stable against itself — they cannot distinguish "output unchanged" from "output changed and the expectations were written to match". Approving on the strength of a green gate here would have been approving a claim the gate does not make.
SETTLED BY RUNNING THE PRE-CHANGE MODULE, which is the only thing that actually decides it:
  materialized `git show 95575b34^:apps/daemon/src/planning/compiled-authority-bodies.ts` as a probe INSIDE the same directory, so its relative imports (`./compiled-authority-contracts.js`, `@moe/core`) resolve exactly as they did before the split;
  copied the CURRENT test verbatim and repointed only its two module imports at that probe — the goldens, fixtures and assertions are byte-identical to the shipped test;
  ran it: **Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 8 passed (8), EXIT 0.**
  The PRE-SPLIT implementation satisfies the CURRENT goldens exactly — canonical plan bytes, canonical acceptance bytes, graph bytes, all four sha256 digests, the three content hashes, byte counts, key ordering, the freezing vector, the refusal paths, and the single-export surface assertion. So the goldens are not post-hoc values fitted to a changed output; the split really is byte-for-byte identical, and the title's claim holds empirically rather than by assertion.
  Probes deleted immediately afterwards; `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/planning` is EMPTY.
EXPORT SURFACE, checked across the split rather than at HEAD only: `git show 95575b34^:…` exposes exactly `export function compiledPlanAuthority`, and HEAD exposes exactly `export function compiledPlanAuthority` at :106. One export before, one export after, same name, same file. The two new modules are internal to the barrel and widen nothing.
PASS.

== 4. DoD 4 — GATES, RE-RUN BY ME (standalone, PIPESTATUS captured) ==
  the exact stored verification command (4 files) => Test Files 4 passed (4) / Tests 22 passed (22), EXIT 0 — identical to the recorded task.verification.
  pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck => EXIT 0 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo present, so it really executed rather than resolving to nothing.
Re-run again after all my mutations were restored: still 4 passed (4) / 22 passed (22), EXIT 0. PASS.

== 5. DoD 5 — MUTATION DRILL ==
Anchor: SHA256 compiled-approval-authority-body.ts = dad081a9363b11bed1488452b5393dfb27f93ce72dd1f657bc5efe5473bfe24f, backed up out of tree.
ONE-BYTE CANONICAL MUTATION at compiled-approval-authority-body.ts:105 — `nodeKind: "LEAF"` -> `nodeKind: "LEAFX"`, `--numstat` 1/1:
  Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8), EXIT 1, and the reds are the right four:
    "pins canonical bytes, digests, ordering, freezing, and its exact public surface"  <- the NAMED assertion the clause requires
    "carries criterion statements byte-equal into the acceptance contract"
    "loads the unchanged public bridge in plain Node and reproduces the canonical digests"
    "PARITY LANE: the real plan.propose seam admits the compiled two-node chain"
  The last two matter beyond the clause: the bridge arm proves the `.js` bridges carry the same bytes through a plain-Node load, and the parity arm proves the goldens bind a REAL `plan.propose` seam rather than only a local fixture. A one-byte change to the serialization is visible at all three levels.
RESTORE PROOF, in a call separate from the restore: SHA256 back to dad081a9…e24f, `git diff --exit-code` clean across all six owned paths, planning porcelain empty, focused gate green again.
DISCLOSING AN ABORTED SECOND DRILL, because a half-run mutation on a shared worktree deserves a record: I also attempted the "order" half of the clause by swapping two adjacent keys in the `applicability` literal. The editor I used rewrote CRLF to LF across the whole file, which contaminated the change far beyond the two lines I intended, so the run would have measured line endings rather than key order. I abandoned it and restored from the backup rather than reporting a result I could not attribute. The clause reads "one-byte/order", so the one-byte drill discharges it; I am recording the abandoned attempt rather than leaving a silent gap.

== 6. THE .js BRIDGES ==
Both are one line, `export * from "./<module>.ts"`, matching this repo's bridge pattern, and the test's plain-Node arm loads them and reproduces the canonical digests — so they are exercised, not decorative. They are declared owned paths and are carried in the completion commit, which is correct for this package.

Approving.
